review_text: A fantastic gateway game. The rules are simple, turns are quick, and everyone stays involved. We had a great time.
The game is enjoyable and the components are attractive. It works well with three players, although the final score felt close to random.
It is neither especially good nor especially bad. The rules are clear, but the game did not leave a strong impression.
The idea is interesting, but the game takes too long and the downtime between turns is frustrating. I would not choose it for a casual evening.
The rulebook is dense and the first game was difficult to understand. Once we learned it, the decisions became rewarding.
This is a challenging strategy game with several interacting systems. Experienced players will enjoy planning several turns ahead.
Building an efficient engine and managing resources are the best parts. The economic theme comes through clearly in every round.
The artwork is beautiful, but the player elimination feels harsh and the game becomes repetitive after several plays.
The game is not difficult to learn, and the turns are not excessively long. It is a relaxed choice for new players.
I expected a deep campaign, but the scenarios are short and the story is barely developed. The components are fine, though.
With two players it feels tense and tactical; with four, the waiting time is noticeable. I am unsure which player count I prefer.

complaints: waiting time increases with four players

review_text: The game looks impressive on the table, and I wanted to like it, but the scoring system is confusing and the ending was anticlimactic.
